question: What are Walmart's lease obligations (operating and finance) and how big are they relative to total assets?

answer.summary: Walmart's total assets as of FY2024 (January 31, 2024) were $252.40B [F00119], up 3.8% YoY [F00120]. The retrieved evidence contains the right-of-use (ROU) ASSET side of leases but does not contain the lease OBLIGATIONS (liabilities) figures. Operating lease ROU assets were $13.67B, equal to 5.4% of total assets [F00111], up from $13.55B in the prior year [F00112]. Finance lease ROU assets were $5.86B, equal to 2.3% of total assets [F00113], up from $4.92B in the prior year [F00114]. By segment, Walmart US was the largest contributor to the asset increase at $137.78B (54.6% of total assets) [F00966], up $7.12B (+5.5%) from $130.66B [F00987], accounting for 77% of the total change. Because the evidence lacks the operating and finance lease liability line items, the ratio of lease obligations to total assets cannot be determined from this evidence.
drivers: By segment, Walmart US assets of $137.78B (54.6% of total) [F00966] rose $7.12B (+5.5%) from $130.66B [F00987], the LARGEST CONTRIBUTOR TO THE CHANGE at 77% of the total asset change.
Corporate And Support assets of $12.80B (5.1% of total) [F00969] rose $2.52B (+24.5%) from $10.28B [F00990], 27% of the total change.
Walmart International assets of $86.14B (34.1% of total) [F00967] fell $630.00M (-0.7%) from $86.77B [F00988], moving AGAINST the total change (offsets 7%).
Sams Club assets of $15.68B (6.2% of total) [F00968] rose $192.00M (+1.2%) from $15.49B [F00989], 2% of the total change.

By component, net property, plant and equipment of $110.81B (43.9% of total) [F00109] rose $10.05B (+10.0%) from $100.76B [F00110], the LARGEST CONTRIBUTOR TO THE CHANGE; its $10.05B swing exceeded the net total change of $9.20B [F00120], so other components offset it (no percentage share is meaningful).
Operating lease ROU assets rose $118.00M (+0.9%) to $13.67B (5.4% of total) [F00111] from $13.55B [F00112], 1% of the total change.
Finance lease ROU assets rose $936.00M (+19.0%) to $5.86B (2.3% of total) [F00113] from $4.92B [F00114], 10% of the total change.
risks_and_red_flags: The lease OBLIGATIONS (operating and finance lease liabilities) are not present in the retrieved evidence, so the requested ratio of lease obligations to total assets cannot be computed.
ROU assets are asset-side balances and are not a substitute for lease liability/obligation figures; they can move differently from the corresponding obligations.
Purchase obligations of $34.3B (of which $14.6B due within one year) are reported separately [T00528] and are not lease obligations.
data_quality_notes: The evidence provides right-of-use ASSET values, not lease OBLIGATIONS (liabilities); the lease liability line items are absent from the retrieved evidence.
Duplicate facts with conflicting values were set aside during parsing, with the primary-statement value kept.
Management lease accounting policy is described in prose [T00662] but contains no obligation amounts.

outlook.actuals_view: FY2024 actuals show total assets of $252.40B [F00119] with operating lease ROU assets of $13.67B [F00111] and finance lease ROU assets of $5.86B [F00113]; Walmart US was the largest segment contributor to the asset change at 77% [F00966].
outlook.forward_looking_guidance: No forward-looking lease obligation guidance is present in the retrieved evidence.

follow_up_checks: Locate the Leases note in the 10-K to extract operating lease liabilities and finance lease liabilities (the obligation side, not ROU assets).
Verify the maturity schedule of undiscounted lease payments for both operating and finance leases.
Check the balance sheet for 'Operating lease liabilities' and 'Finance lease liabilities' line items and reconcile to the lease note.
Confirm whether the $34.3B purchase obligations [T00528] include any lease commitments.
